instruction: Independent visual/content recheck after a user-reported canonical repair. Inspect the complete composed scenes and all ten questions for exp26-u13-001, plus the grammar repair exp26-u13-010-q1. Confirm puck placement agrees with rim/side-board wording, retrieval orientation, actor references, and exact final hashes. This is a review packet; do not edit the bank.

scenarios.title: Read the rim before reaching it
scenarios.objective: Notice the forechecker before collecting a rim.
scenarios.briefing: YOU are approaching a loose rim. Gold 1 is closing from the middle. D2 waits behind the puck as a possible outlet. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The puck marker is separate from every player near the side boards.
YOU are approaching a loose rim. Gold 1 is closing from the middle. D2 waits behind the puck as a possible outlet.

sources.title: Developing Skilled Defencemen — Overview
sources.use: Supports the stated coaching principle. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

scenarios.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Where is the puck at this freeze?
questions.explanation: The puck marker is separate from every player near the side boards.

questions.prompt: Which two pieces of information help before this pickup?

options.text: Whether D2 can offer an outlet

questions.explanation: Pressure and support shape the first read; they do not guarantee a specific pass.

questions.prompt: Order one preparation routine for this rim.

options.text: Control the puck and reassess the outlet

questions.explanation: This is a suggested routine; scanning may happen repeatedly.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a pickup position that preserves a view of Gold 1.
questions.explanation: A position inside the rim can allow a check of pressure. Another angle may suit the puck’s actual travel.

questions.prompt: Suppose Gold 1 now reaches the wall first. What deserves a fresh look?

options.text: Contain and support rather than assume you own the puck
Continue the planned outlet as though possession is secure
Leave for a rush before seeing the puck

questions.explanation: A contested pickup changes the job. The exact response depends on support and reach.

questions.prompt: What would you look at twice while retrieving this rim?
questions.explanation: Explain how the forechecker or outlet may move between the first scan and the pickup.

questions.prompt: Which new fact would make the planned pickup less certain?

options.text: Gold 1 reaches the rim before YOU
W stays higher in the zone

questions.explanation: Gold 1 reaching the rim changes possession risk, so YOU must protect and support; if YOU arrives first with control, the outlet scan returns.

questions.prompt: Which two words would make the next call useful?

options.text: Call for a pass without naming a lane

questions.explanation: A pressure-side call and support status give teammates actionable information; a vague pass call does not say what changed.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an approach angle that keeps the loose rim and Gold 1 in view.
questions.explanation: The offset approach preserves a view of both puck and forechecker; if Gold 1 crosses the lane, slow and support rather than reaching blind.

questions.prompt: How would you decide whether to collect or contain at the rim?
questions.explanation: Compare who can reach the puck, Gold 1’s route and D2’s support before committing; if the opponent arrives first, contain and wait for help.

scenarios.title: Be available near the net before the shot
scenarios.objective: Recognize a receiving or deflection area without prescribing a net battle.
scenarios.briefing: F1 has the puck high near the side boards. YOU are beside Gold’s net on the same side. This non-contact recognition exercise asks YOU to become visible near the front before a possible shot or pass. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: YOU are beside Gold’s net, away from the middle of the ice.
F1 has the puck high near the side boards. YOU are beside Gold’s net on the same side. This non-contact recognition exercise asks YOU to become visible near the front before a possible shot or pass.

sources.use: Supports age/topic placement only. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

scenarios.limits: U13 recognition-only net-front exercise. No contested net battles, screening-contact rules or tip execution are certified. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Where are YOU compared with the net-front centre?

options.text: Behind F1 in the neutral zone
Beside the net, toward the side boards

questions.explanation: YOU are beside Gold’s net, away from the middle of the ice.

questions.prompt: Which two things should you check before presenting near the front?

options.text: Whether standing on the goalie guarantees a goal

questions.explanation: Availability requires a view and useful separation. This exercise does not authorize contact with a goalie.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possible preparation for a front-of-net option.

options.text: Find available space near the front
Present the stick and watch the puck

questions.explanation: This is a recognition routine; movement and stick skill require on-ice practice.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an example receiving position near the front.
questions.explanation: The reference illustrates a different side of Gold 1. Other safe, visible receiving spots may work.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 follows and closes the route, what could help?

options.text: Assume the same pass remains open

questions.explanation: Another pocket or a delayed arrival may help; no static point is guaranteed open.

questions.prompt: What should F1 be able to see before trying to involve YOU?
questions.explanation: A recognizable target and a route that is not simply through the defender; timing also matters.

questions.prompt: Why is YOU beside the net rather than already in the slot?

options.text: The scene asks YOU to become visible near the front
The puck is loose behind the net

questions.explanation: The exercise states the recognition task is to become visible near the front; if the puck or defender moves, choose a new lane.

questions.prompt: Which two details should F1 see before involving YOU?

options.text: Whether F1 can shoot through Gold 1 without changing the angle

questions.explanation: F1 needs your reachable route and the defender’s coverage to choose; no net outcome is guaranteed from the freeze.

questions.prompt: Move YOU from the side of the net into a visible net-front lane outside Gold 1.
questions.explanation: The position makes YOU visible without standing on Gold 1’s body line; if Gold 1 closes, slide to a separate support lane.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between being near the net and being useful near the net?
questions.explanation: A useful spot changes the goalie’s sightline or offers a reachable pass while preserving separation; if it blocks F1’s lane, proximity alone does not help.
